theorem_obligations.intent: Show that `ShrB32Step` gives at most one post-state for fixed pre-state/instruction.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For every state `s` and instruction `i`, if `ShrB32Step s i s1` and `ShrB32Step s i s2`, then `s1 = s2`.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem shrB32Step_deterministic (s : MachineState) (i : ShrB32Instruction) (s1 s2 : MachineState) (h1 : ShrB32Step s i s1) (h2 : ShrB32Step s i s2) : s1 = s2
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: Relational constructors include `executed`, `guardFalse`, and `malformed`; no additional assumptions.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Branch-level constructors enforce distinct post-state shapes and the relation cannot be satisfied by vacuous alternatives for fixed preconditions.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Case split on `h1` and `h2`; constructor mismatches close by contradiction with branch equations; matching constructors reduce to definitional equality on updated states.

theorem_obligations.intent: Relate executable outcomes to exact relational constructors, and for each `ShrB32Step` constructor, force the unique corresponding `execShrB32` branch, with malformed guarded by non-false predicate state.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words:
(a) `execShrB32` returning `guardFalse s'` implies a `guardFalse` relation step.
(b) `execShrB32` returning `executed s'` implies an `executed` relation step with matching source witness values.
(c) `execShrB32` returning `malformed s'` implies a `malformed` relation step and `evalGuard s i.guard ≠ some false`.
(d) `ShrB32Step` to `execShrB32` constructor mapping is explicit: a `guardFalse` step forces `execShrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s')`; an `executed` step forces `execShrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s')`; a `malformed` step forces `(evalGuard s i.guard = some false -> execShrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s'))` and `(evalGuard s i.guard ≠ some false -> execShrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.malformed s'))`.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem execShrB32_sound_guardFalse ...
  (s : MachineState) (i : ShrB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState)
  (h : execShrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s')) : ShrB32Step s i s'

theorem execShrB32_sound_executed ...

theorem execShrB32_sound_malformed ...

theorem shrB32Step_to_exec_correspondence (s : MachineState) (i : ShrB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState) (hstep : ShrB32Step s i s') :
  (∃ h : evalGuard s i.guard = some false, execShrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s')) ∨
  (∃ va vb : B32, ShrB32Step.executed s i va vb ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ = hstep ∧ execShrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s')) ∨
  (evalGuard s i.guard ≠ some false ∧ execShrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.malformed s'))
hypotheses: h : execShrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s')
h : execShrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s')
h : execShrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.malformed s')
theorem_obligations.conclusion: Executable outcomes and relational constructors are synchronized branch-for-branch; malformed relation is separated from false-guard behavior.
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: Architecture-approved executable/relational split in this unit; this obligation requires constructor-level correspondence including malformed/falsity disambiguation.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The mapping now names exact outcome constructors and adds a disambiguation condition so malformed and false-guard branches cannot be merged by an existential.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold both definitions. For (a/b/c), split on `execShrB32` branches and use constructor inversions. For (d), split on `hstep`; guardFalse and executed are direct, while malformed is split by `evalGuard` equality/inequality to choose guard-false or malformed outcome. This exposes ambiguity and enforces synchronization.

theorem_obligations.intent: Characterize exactly when the executable outcome is `malformed` and show the stored state is unchanged.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: `execShrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.malformed s')` iff `((evalGuard s i.guard = none) ∨ (evalGuard s i.guard = some true ∧ (readSource s i.a = none ∨ readSource s i.b = none))) ∧ s' = s`.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem execShrB32_malformed_iff_malformed_condition (s : MachineState) (i : ShrB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState) :
    execShrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.malformed s') ↔ ((evalGuard s i.guard = none ∨ (evalGuard s i.guard = some true ∧ (readSource s i.a = none ∨ readSource s i.b = none))) ∧ s' = s)
theorem_obligations.conclusion: Exact malformed-branch characterization for this `Option`-valued executable model.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The right-hand side is satisfiable by concrete partial states (missing predicate or missing source reads), so the theorem is not vacuous.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold `execShrB32`, split on `evalGuard` and source lookups; use constructor injectivity for `ExecOutcome.malformed` and arithmetic simplification of `Fin` modulo construction.

theorem_obligations.intent: On guard true with both source operands available and register destination, show exact right-shift semantics in post-state.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: If `evalGuard s i.guard = some true`, `i.d = Destination.reg r`, `readSource s i.a = some va`, and `readSource s i.b = some vb`, then there exists `s'` such that `execShrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s')` and `s'.valueRegs r = some (shrB32Value va vb)`.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem execShrB32_shr_fidelity (s : MachineState) (i : ShrB32Instruction) (r : RegId) (va vb : B32)
    (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true) (hd : i.d = Destination.reg r)
    (ha : readSource s i.a = some va) (hb : readSource s i.b = some vb) :
    ∃ s' : MachineState, execShrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') ∧ s'.valueRegs r = some (shrB32Value va vb)
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true
ha : readSource s i.a = some va
hb : readSource s i.b = some vb
theorem_obligations.conclusion: `valueRegs r` in the executed post-state equals `shrB32Value va vb`.
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: Semantics `d = a >> b` plus clamped amount and bounded zero-fill behavior are encoded as `shrB32Value`.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The conclusion constrains the exact written value and therefore excludes degenerate/no-op or alternate shift implementations.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold `execShrB32`, rewrite by hypotheses to force executed branch, and simplify `updateDestination` at a register destination.

theorem_obligations.intent: Show that bounded execution only updates the chosen destination register and never predicate registers.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For any `ShrB32Step s i s'` and register destination `r`, every predicate-register component is preserved and every value register except possibly `r` is preserved from `s` to `s'`.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem shrB32Step_destination_only_frame
  (s : MachineState) (i : ShrB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState) (r : RegId)
  (hstep : ShrB32Step s i s') (hd : i.d = Destination.reg r) :
  (∀ r' : RegId, r' ≠ r -> s'.valueRegs r' = s.valueRegs r') /\ (∀ p : PredId, s'.predRegs p = s.predRegs p)
theorem_obligations.conclusion: No state components outside destination register are modified.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Nontrivial because executed, guard-false, and malformed branches differ in read/write effect; this theorem identifies the exact framed writes for all branches.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Split on `hstep`; `guardFalse`/`malformed` are reflexive state equalities, and `executed` follows from the updateDestination definition.
